headline: Napa Valley Thermal Springs and Estate Reservations
reservation: While the town itself is public, specific mud bath treatments and geothermal mineral pools at historic resorts require advanced bookings. Most premium wineries in the northern Napa Valley now operate on a prior-appointment basis; check individual estate websites for tasting room availability and seasonal tour schedules.

days.title: Geothermal and Historic Heritage

stops.name: Old Faithful Geyser of California
stops.detail: Witness the regular eruptions of this geothermal feature, one of only three 'faithful' geysers in the world.

stops.name: Petrified Forest
stops.detail: Walk among ancient redwood trees turned to stone by volcanic ash from an eruption of Mount Saint Helena.

days.driving: Allow 45 minutes; sights are clustered at the northern end of the valley.
days.note: The geyser interval varies; allow time for at least one full cycle.

days.title: Volcanic Slopes and Vintages

stops.name: Castello di Amorosa
stops.detail: Explore a meticulously recreated 13th-century Italian castle dedicated to traditional winemaking methods.

stops.name: Sterling Vineyards Aerial Tram
stops.detail: Ascend the hillside via tram for panoramic views of the northern valley and the surrounding Palisades.

days.driving: Allow 30 minutes; wineries are located along Highway 29 and Silverado Trail.
days.note: Reservations for castle tours are essential and often book out weeks in advance.

days.title: Outdoor Heights and Mud Baths
days.start: Suggested: 8:30 AM from Robert Louis Stevenson State Park

stops.name: Mount Saint Helena Trailhead
stops.detail: Hike the initial miles of the trail for views of the Bay Area and the site where Stevenson spent his honeymoon.

stops.name: Indian Springs Art Deco Pool
stops.detail: Conclude the trip with a soak in the historic mineral pool fed by local thermal geysers.

days.driving: Allow 1 hour total; the trailhead is a short drive north on Highway 29.
days.note: State park access is daylight only; thermal pool access depends on resort guest status or day passes.

intel.title: Downtown Hubs
intel.text: Public parking is available near Lincoln Avenue, though spaces fill during the Saturday market. Most wineries provide dedicated guest parking on-site.

intel.title: Valley Coverage
intel.text: Cell service is strong in Calistoga but can be intermittent on the higher trails of Mount Saint Helena. Lodge Wi-Fi is standard for navigating valley itineraries.

intel.title: Northern Outpost
intel.text: Calistoga is the final fuel stop before heading north toward Lake County or deeper into the mountains. Prices in the valley are typically higher than in Santa Rosa.

intel.title: Harvest Rhythm
intel.text: September and October bring heavy traffic to Highway 29 due to grape harvesting equipment. Plan for longer transit times between tastings during this window.

intel.title: Resort Privacy
intel.text: Many thermal springs are located on private resort property. Verify if day-use access is permitted or if a spa treatment is required for entry.

plan.arrival: Pick up a vehicle at Sonoma County Airport, drive east through the hills, and secure a reservation at a historic inn on the Silverado Trail.
plan.vehicle: A standard passenger car is ideal for the paved valley roads; RVs may find the winding Highway 29 north toward Clear Lake challenging.
plan.goldenHour: The Palisades rock formation east of town glows deep orange at sunset, best viewed from the valley floor.
